forensic_findings.title: All 15 official `nvthanh2004` notebooks (`11 GDUT_V2 + 4 Baselines`) share the exact SHA-256 dataset digest (`ce2a883e0b50...`) and 48/48 matched Stage 2 hyperparameters.
forensic_findings.detail: Replaces all legacy experimental baselines. On identical 1,587-image Official Test (`ce2a883e` Stage 1 protocol), `A6_yolo11s` reaches `88.94% mAP50 / 58.08% mAP50-95` (`9,476,783` deploy fused params, `15.207 ms` T4 FP32), outperforming `B1 (YOLO11n-DCRCF)` (`84.85% / 54.77%`, `+4.09 / +3.31 pp`) and `B2 (YOLOv8s-DWR-ASPP-NWD)` (`87.51% / 56.59%`, `+1.43 / +1.50 pp`, `-41.8%` deploy params, `-32.1%` T4 latency). Even `A6_yolov8s` (`88.37% / 57.37%`) beats both `B1` and `B2`.

forensic_findings.title: Fused deploy parameter count (`9,476,783` vs `9,487,583`) reconciled mathematically (`10,800` Conv-BN folding params).
forensic_findings.detail: In `Baseline_A6_Comparison.ipynb`, `A6_yolo11s` calls BOTH `switch_to_deploy()` AND `model.fuse()` (folding Conv2d+BatchNorm2d = `-10,800` affine parameters), producing `9,476,783` deployed parameters (`15.207 ms` T4 FP32); calling `switch_to_deploy()` alone yields `9,487,583` parameters (`-300,992` from `RepConv`).

forensic_findings.title: Paper-to-GDUT cross-domain gaps documented from `paper_vs_experiment.csv` (`B1 -7.85 / -5.83 pp`, `B2 -4.49 / -5.61 pp`).
forensic_findings.detail: Both peer-reviewed detectors suffer sharp drops moving from 2-class SHWD to deduplicated 5-class GDUT Test: B1 recalls drop `-12.02 pp` (Test `none` AP50 = `78.3%`, R = `68.0%`) due to `26.22%` neck transfer discontinuity (`78` newly initialized tensors), while B2 inflates parameters to `16,275,615` fused (`22.396 ms` T4 FP32).
